subject: Incident briefing: November 17 service interruption — timeline & action plan
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>
To: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@optimahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Briefing: November 17 service interruption — initial summary and next steps

Jacob —

Thank you for the patience while our team investigated last night’s disruption to model-serving in us-west. I wanted to send a short update with what we know now and the immediate actions we took. We will follow up with a full RCA document by Friday, Nov 20.

What happened (brief):
- 11/17 01:03 UTC: elevated latency and dropped requests for a subset of customer routes running the rwd-1-large variant.
- 11/17 01:10 UTC: automated routing fallback engaged; traffic moved to healthy model variants to reduce errors.
- 11/17 01:22 UTC: root cause identified (intermittent GPU driver memory leak under a rare attention pattern).
- 11/17 01:45 UTC: mitigation applied (rolling process restart and driver patch); service returned to baseline by 02:05 UTC.

Immediate customer impact: brief request errors (5xx) and increased tail latency for ~45 minutes. Based on our logs your traffic experienced ~0.9% error rate during the window; we will include per-route counts in the formal RCA.

What we did for OptimaHealth:
- Prioritized your production pools for the rolling restarts.
- Retained all request traces and KV cache snapshots for post-incident analysis.
- Opened this thread to share milestones and the formal RCA when ready.

Next steps:
- Interim update (this message) — ACTION: none required from you.
- Full RCA and timeline delivered by Fri, Nov 20 (PDF + CSV timeline) — ACTION: review and flag any follow-ups.
- If you need an earlier technical walkthrough or formal exec briefing, I can schedule time with our reliability lead.

Attachments: (will be included in the RCA) 20261120-optimahealth-rca.pdf (draft), service-timeline-20261117.csv

Sincerely,
Kimberly Park
Account Director, Enterprise Growth
Redwood Inference
From: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@optimahealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Briefing: November 17 service interruption — initial summary and next steps

Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick note. A few quick questions from our side:
1) Can you confirm the exact time window OptimaHealth saw failed requests and whether any inferencing payloads were dropped (we rely on those traces for audit)?
2) We need a preliminary estimate for potential SLA credits — what is Redwood’s approach for this class of incident?
3) Can you share whether any customer data was written to disk or exported during the event?

We may also loop in procurement if there’s a credit conversation.

Regards,
Jacob
Director of Platform Engineering
OptimaHealth
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Briefing: November 17 service interruption — initial summary and next steps

Kimberly / Marissa —

Drafting the RCA now. Notes for the customer doc:
- Include per-route error counts (CSV) and per-customer tail latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99).
- Call out root cause as a driver-level memory leak triggered by a particular multi-query attention pattern; link kernel traces.
- Confirmed no disk writes of customer payloads; KV caches were in-memory only and persisted only to our encrypted backup snapshots — no external export.
- SLA credit guidance: incidents where service is unavailable beyond SLO window default to pro-rata credit; will include a preliminary credit calculation for OptimaHealth based on affected tokens and uptime window.

I’ll attach the draft timeline and the kernel trace excerpt. Kimberly, want me to include a one-page summary for execs that focuses on risk mitigation items?

—Marcus
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>
To: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@optimahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 12:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Final RCA & action plan — Nov 17 us-west service disruption (OptimaHealth impact)

Jacob —

Please find attached our formal RCA for the Nov 17 us-west service disruption (attachment: 20261120-optimahealth-rca.pdf). Below is an executive summary, the timeline we reconstructed, customer-specific impact, and our concrete commitments.

Executive summary:
- Impact window (OptimaHealth): 2026-11-17 01:03:12 UTC — 2026-11-17 02:05:47 UTC.
- Scope: requests routed to rwd-1-large model variant in us-west; OptimaHealth experienced a peak error rate of 0.9% and elevated p99 latency during the window.
- Root cause: an intermittent GPU driver memory leak exposed by a rarely-seen attention pattern in multi-query requests; the leak caused per-process memory growth and eventual OOMs that triggered service restarts.
- Data exposure: confirmed none. No customer payloads were written to disk or exfiltrated. KV cache snapshots remain encrypted and were not exported.

Detailed timeline (high level):
- 2026-11-17 01:03:12 UTC — Monitoring alerts: increased errors in several pools.
- 2026-11-17 01:09:48 UTC — Automated routing fallback moved 74% of traffic to healthy variants.
- 2026-11-17 01:22:31 UTC — Engineering identified driver memory growth correlated with a specific attention micro-pattern.
- 2026-11-17 01:33:05 UTC — Hotfix (driver patch + controlled process restarts) prepared and rolled.
- 2026-11-17 01:45:12 UTC — Rollout commenced (staggered across hosts to minimize disruption).
- 2026-11-17 02:05:47 UTC — Metrics returned to baseline and routing normalized.

Customer impact & SLA credits:
- Per our SLA, we will provide a pro-rata credit for affected time and error rate. Preliminary estimate: we will calculate credits based on affected token volume during the window; draft credit sheet is in the attached RCA. Procurement (cc’d) may follow up on details.

Remediation & commitments (what we are doing):
1) Short term (complete): patched driver and rolled restarts to remove leaking processes.
2) Near term (2 weeks): add an automated health-check that detects this memory-growth signature and proactively drains affected containers before OOMs.
3) Mid term (90 days): model-serving runtime update to hard-limit per-process GPU allocations and add kernel-level mitigation for the attention micro-pattern.
4) Long term: expanded chaos testing of attention pattern combinations in our pre-prod harness.

Requested customer actions (if any):
- None required to remediate. If OptimaHealth wants a confidential technical walkthrough, we can schedule a 60-minute session with Marcus and the reliability team next week.

Attachments included: 20261120-optimahealth-rca.pdf (formal RCA, includes CSV timeline and per-route metrics), service-timeline-20261117.csv (per-route event log).

If you’d like us to prepare an executive one-pager or to open a formal credit request ticket, say the word and we’ll proceed.

Thanks again for your partnership and patience — happy to hop on a call.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Account Director, Enterprise Growth
Redwood Inference
